chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when they had fasting to make up, would delay it until the month of Sha'ban—out of reluctance to prevent the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from having his need from them—so when Sha'ban arrived, they would fast, and he would fast with them.
He said, "And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say, 'Sha'ban is my month.'"

key_terms.شَعْبَانُ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)

ai.seo_question: Why did the wives of the Prophet delay making up fasts until Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical wisdom of the Prophet's wives in balancing religious obligations with marital duties, specifically delaying *qada'* fasts to Sha'ban to avoid the potential neglect of conjugal rights during Ramadan. The Prophet’s declaration, 'Sha'ban is my month,' underscores the month's significance as a spiritual preparation for Ramadan, a theme widely discussed in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the Prophet's personal devotion and the virtue of fasting in this intercalary month.
